problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: Can the cycle lemma be applied to prove the Chung-Feller theorem: the number of lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(2n,0)$ with exactly $k$ upsteps above the $x$-axis is $\binom{2n}{n}/(n+1)$, independent.

currentState.nextAction: Prove that rotation orbit cut at 1-positions gives n+1 balanced paths with distinct types

upsteps_above_below_disjoint: above/below axis filters are disjoint (PROVED)
Computational verification: upstep partition for n=2 paths (native_decide)
insights: catalan_formula (Cn n * (n+1) = C(2n,n)) proved in BallotProblemOQ03.lean:523
Chung-Feller theorem: paths from (0,0) to (2n,0) with k upsteps above x-axis = C_n, independent of k
Proof via cycle lemma: (1::l) has exactly 1 good rotation. Each rotation orbit at 1-positions gives n+1 balanced paths.
Key remaining challenge: proving different cut positions in rotation orbit yield different upstep-above-axis counts
Cyclic rotation does NOT simply shift type by ±1 — the change depends on the full prefix sum structure
The bijection between rotation index and type requires careful tracking of how heights shift
nextSteps: Prove rotation orbit has exactly n+1 balanced paths (from n+1 positions with value 1 in the augmented sequence)
Prove types are all distinct within each orbit (the hard step — requires prefix sum tracking)
Alternative: construct explicit bijection between adjacent types via tunnel/arch decomposition
Consider Aristotle companion file for routine supporting lemmas
